# Helping Your Midwife Find You

*A short guide from your Riverside community midwives*

Hello! I'm one of your Riverside midwives, and I was asked to write this page because I am the one who gets lost the most. Nobody knows better than me how many ways there are to miss a front door.

Where I come from in the Philippines, we say the midwife is like family. That is how we want to arrive at your house: like a friend who has come to help. A friend who is, ideally, not driving round the block for the third time at 3am.

So here is how you can help us find you fast.

## First, the 37 weeks rule

Home birth cover starts from **37 weeks**. Before 37 weeks, if labour starts, please go to the hospital. We tell everyone this at the booking visit, but there is a lot to remember at that visit, so here it is again. Stick it on the fridge.

## Who is coming

**Two midwives** come for a home birth, and we usually come in two separate cars. If you can, please keep **two parking spaces** free near your house.

We also carry a lot: gas and air cylinders, the big bag, and sometimes the birthing pool things. By the time we reach your door our arms are very tired, so a short walk from the car makes us very happy.

**Parking permits:** In some areas, like Anfield and Kensington, you need a permit to park. We have had tickets before, and nobody wants a parking ticket at a birth. Please ask the council for a visitor permit, or keep one ready to put on the dashboard.

## Calling us when labour starts

1. Phone the **Riverside birth line: [BIRTH LINE NUMBER]**. Save it in your phone now, not at 3am.
2. Please do not call my personal mobile. The birth line goes to whoever is on call, so you always get someone who is ready for you.
3. Tell us your name and address. If your home is tricky to find (see below), tell us that too.
4. Send us your location. You can use the **what3words** app, or just send a **pin on WhatsApp** to the birth line phone. It takes a minute and it works very well.

**If you think it is an emergency, call 999.**

## Tales of a lost midwife

I promise these are all true.

**The flats in Everton.** I was looking for flat 14. Flat 13 was right there, so flat 14 must be next door, yes? No. Flat 14 was in a completely different building. I drove round and round for 20 minutes. In the end I spotted a dad waving a tea towel out of a window like he was rescuing me from a desert island. He did rescue me.
*Lesson: if you live in a block of flats, tell us which building, and which entrance to use.*

**The house with no number.** One house had only a name, no number, in a long street of terraces that all look the same. My sat nav was very sure of itself and took me to a chip shop. The chips smelled lovely, but it was not the right place.
*Lesson: if your house has a name and no number, send us a pin.*

**The wrong house.** Once I walked into the wrong house because the door was open. A very nice old man was sitting there. He did not call the police. He gave me a Jammie Dodger. I did not find the baby, but it was a good biscuit.
*Lesson: a front door that is open is not a clue. Someone should be waiting to welcome us.*

**The balloons.** One family tied balloons to their gate, like for a party. It was the best idea ever. I saw them from the end of the street and found the house straight away. It is a birth, so it really is a party!
*Lesson: balloons work. Please copy this family.*

## Make your house easy to spot

- **Put the porch light on at night.** Please, please. In winter, dark streets all look the same, and a light is like a little lighthouse for us.
- **Make your number easy to read**, or tie balloons or something bright to the gate.
- **Choose a "door person".** This is someone who watches for us and opens the door, so we do not have to knock and wait. A tea towel at the window is also fine.
- **Do not trust the sat nav 100%.** Sat navs are good, but they have taken me to a chip shop.

## Inside the house

Once we are at the door, the next job is to get in with all our bags safely.

- **Clear the stairs and the hallway.** We are carrying heavy things, and we cannot always see our feet. Please move the shoes, the washing basket and the Lego. Lego on the floor is the enemy of a tired midwife.
- **Pets in another room, please.** I love dogs. I really do. One very friendly staffie loved me so much that he jumped on me every visit, and one day I nearly dropped the gas and air. A dog in another room with a toy or a treat is better for everybody, including the dog. During the pushing, I need my full attention on you and the baby.

Your home does not need to be perfectly tidy. We have seen everything, and we are not here to judge. We only need a clear path and a safe space.

## Fridge checklist

Tick each box as you do it, then stick this on the fridge.

- ☐ I know home birth cover starts at **37 weeks**. Before that, I go to the hospital.
- ☐ The Riverside birth line number is saved in my phone (and my partner's phone).
- ☐ I have the what3words address, or I know how to send a WhatsApp pin.
- ☐ I have a visitor permit sorted, or one ready for the dashboard (if I live in a permit area).
- ☐ There is room for **two cars** near the house, if possible.
- ☐ The porch light will be on at night.
- ☐ My house number is easy to see, or I have balloons ready for the gate.
- ☐ Someone is the "door person" who will watch for the midwives.
- ☐ Pets have a plan: who takes them, and which room they go in.
- ☐ The stairs and hallway are clear: no shoes, no washing basket, no Lego.
- ☐ If it is an emergency, I will call **999**.

## See you soon

We are really looking forward to meeting you and your new baby. If you have any questions about this page, ask us at your next visit.

And if we do get lost, please wave a tea towel. It works.

*With love from your Riverside community midwives*

---

A few things for you to check before it goes out:

- **Birth line number:** I left a placeholder, so please fill it in.
- **The 999 line:** I added this myself, as it wasn't in your notes. Please check with Deb that she's happy with it.
- **Names and details:** I left out Pippin's name, "Rosemary Cottage" and the Everton block, because families might recognise themselves. If those families are happy, I can put them back in.
- **Permits:** I kept it general and didn't name the council's process. If you have a link or phone number for the visitor permits, add it in.
